stem: A hotel-booking company's data team needs to offload read-heavy nightly reporting queries from its primary RDS instance so those reports stop competing with live booking writes.

choices.text: Enable a Multi-AZ standby for the primary instance and send the reporting queries to it
Vertically resize the primary instance so it has enough headroom for both writes and reports
Create a read replica and point the nightly reporting queries at it
Run the reporting queries against the primary instance, but only during its lowest-traffic hours

rationale: Creating a read replica gives the reporting workload its own asynchronous, read-only copy of the data, which is exactly how a read replica is meant to offload read-heavy traffic from the primary. A Multi-AZ standby replicates synchronously purely for automatic failover and, on a standard RDS instance, is not available to serve read traffic, so it does not solve the offload problem. Vertically resizing the primary instance can add headroom, but it still runs both the writes and the reports on the same instance, so the two workloads keep competing for its resources. Restricting the reports to low-traffic hours reduces contention but does not remove it, and it does not scale if reporting needs to run more often or the low-traffic window shrinks.
